subject: ACME POC: evaluation criteria, timelines, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Howard <alex.howard@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC: evaluation criteria, timelines, and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same frame for the POC:

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: prove Redwood reduces inference cost by >40% for your customer-facing summarization pipeline while keeping F1 and hallucination rates within your tolerance.
- Key stakeholders: Alex (product), Priya (engineering), Ben (procurement), Marissa (sales), Dylan (solutions).

Proposed success criteria (we discussed):
1) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 600ms for 2k token contexts under representative load.
2) Cost: end-to-end per-token cost reduction >= 40% vs current baseline within the trial window.
3) Quality: automated metric thresholds (ROUGE-L and task-specific F1) plus manual review — target: no more than 7% critical failures (hallucinations that change meaning).

Evaluation approach (open for alignment):
- Offline evals: run your historical corpus through model variants and compute metrics (Dylan to own).
- Online shadow: shadow traffic for a 2-week window to validate production behavior (Priya to own infra sandbox).
- Human grading: sample 200 outputs, 3-judge rubric for safety/accuracy (Rachel to coordinate).

Next steps / timeline (proposed):
- Wed 6/2: Redwood sends evaluation rubric + baseline run plan (attached).
- Fri 6/4: ACME provides representative dataset and access details (S3 link)
- Week of 6/7: Offline runs and initial metric review
- Week of 6/14: Shadow testing and human grading

Attachments: poc-timeline-v1.xlsx, acme-poc-success-criteria.docx (first drafts)

Action items:
- Alex: confirm the dataset and any redacted fields by EOD Friday.
- Priya: confirm sandbox IP allowlist + access method.
- Dylan/Rachel: will prep rubric and offline run plan.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the rubric and a concrete timeline.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

Also, can you share an example rubric for human grading so our product team can calibrate? Would prefer a simple 1-5 severity scale per item.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex

Alex / team — attaching the evaluation rubric and an offline-run checklist. High-level notes:

- Offline vs online: recommend doing both. Offline gives fast signal on metric deltas across model variants; online shadow validates real-time failure modes and latency under real sequencing/batching effects.
- Rubric: we used a 1-5 grading scale across three axes: Accuracy (semantic correctness), Safety (harmful / hallucination), Relevance (task fit). A score <= 2 on Accuracy is a critical fail.
- Sampling: for human grading sample 200 items across short/long prompts and edge-cases. 3 independent raters, majority rule; include a calibration batch of 25 items.

See attached: acme-eval-rubric.xlsx (rubric + scoring script), acme-offline-run-checklist.md (checklist).

Proposed owners:
- Dylan: offline runs + metric dashboard setup
- Rachel: organize human grading + calibration session
- Priya: sandbox infra + shadow routing rules
- Alex: sign-off on rubric and dataset

I’ll schedule a 30-min calibration call next Tue; suggest Tue 6/8 10:00am PT.

-Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
